summary: Douglas County lookout site since 1925; the steel tower standing now dates to 1979, is available for emergencies only, and is not open to the public.

facts.design: 14'x14' flattop cab with catwalk on a steel tower

access.note: Listed as not accessible to the public; firelookout.com says it is now available for emergencies.

events.note: Tree lookout (a crow's nest in a Douglas-fir) put into service on the point
L-4 cab on a short timber tower; firelookout.com dates a 20-foot wooden tower to 1933
Army asked for a yearlong observation post; station active October 1942 to October 1943
50-foot timber tower with an Amort-style cab erected about 1.5 miles east; old tower removed
Steel tower from the dismantled Shivigny Mountain lookout installed with a new cabin

corrections.why: 6.1 m is 20 feet, which matches the 1933 wooden tower firelookout.com describes. The present steel tower is 54 feet 6 inches per the register (50 feet per firelookout.com).
L-4 was the cab of the 1934 tower. The register describes the cab on the present steel tower as a 14'x14' flattop with catwalk.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's built year of 1953 is for the 50-foot timber tower erected on a point about 1.5 miles east. The steel tower standing now was installed in 1979, and the site has had a lookout since the 1925 tree lookout.

notes_for_editor: Sources conflict on the 1933/1934 tower (10 vs 20 ft), the present tower height (50 vs 54 ft 6 in), and current status (register says active service; firelookout.com says emergencies only). Staffing as_of is undated. Elevation: record 793.1 m matches the register's 2,602 ft; Cheryl Hill lists 2,866 ft. Access is set to restricted from the Cheryl Hill column; confirm with the Douglas FPA before any visit advice.
